title: The Shutdown Ends, Burry’s New AI Warning & Disney Stumbles | The Weekly Wrap
summary: The November 14 wrap weighs Burry depreciation concerns, emphasizes real returns on AI spending and reviews CoreWeave execution, Disney legacy drag and Circle expectations. It identifies announced deal volume as a forward indicator for advisory activity.
assessment: The depreciation arithmetic is valid under a simple assumption, but dismissing measurement concerns entirely would go too far. Most earnings observations are contemporary diagnoses and several future targets belong to management or consensus. The report does not score personal health disclosures.
framework_points: Separate accounting timing from actual cash economics.
Watch construction execution as well as contracted demand.
Distinguish legacy-business decline from new-business growth.
Use announced deal volume to assess future advisory activity.
transcript_cautions: Personal health information is excluded from the investment claim scorecard.
Disney EPS comparison is garbled in captions; exact numerical direction is not scored from the corrupted wording.
speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman presents; speaker attribution follows the full dialogue.

claims.claim: The shutdown agreement reduces immediate uncertainty but does not permanently settle funding disputes.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track actual funding expiration and subsequent legislation.
claims.reason: This is a conditional political-risk observation rather than a dated forecast of another shutdown.
claims.next_check: Track actual funding expiration and subsequent legislation.

claims.claim: Rising subprime auto delinquencies indicate significant stress in weaker borrowers.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare the original sample, seasonal pattern and broader loan populations.
claims.reason: The quoted Fitch series is a selected securitized subprime sample and was not independently inspected here. It should not be relabeled as all auto borrowers.
claims.next_check: Compare the original sample, seasonal pattern and broader loan populations.

claims.claim: Extending a $75 billion asset useful life from three to six years cuts annual straight-line depreciation from $25 billion to $12.5 billion.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Use asset-level additions, residuals and in-service timing.
claims.reason: The arithmetic is correct for a single fully depreciable cohort with zero residual value and a full year in service. Actual capex includes assets with different lives and start dates.
claims.next_check: Use asset-level additions, residuals and in-service timing.

assumptions: One $75 billion cohort, zero residual value, straight-line depreciation and full-year service.
proof.proof: Annual depreciation is cost divided by useful life: 75/3=25 and 75/6=12.5 billion; pretax accounting earnings differ by 12.5 billion before other effects.
proof.derivation: Annual depreciation is cost divided by useful life: 75/3=25 and 75/6=12.5 billion; pretax accounting earnings differ by 12.5 billion before other effects.

claims.claim: Burry estimates useful-life changes will overstate Meta and Oracle earnings by 21% and 27% by 2028.
claims.speaker: Michael Burry, reported by Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare economic lives, retirements, impairments and the original model.
claims.reason: This is explicitly Burry research, not Eisman own estimate. The 2028 horizon and asset-life assumptions remain unresolved.
claims.next_check: Compare economic lives, retirements, impairments and the original model.

claims.claim: Actual AI returns and cost savings matter more than depreciation choices, so the accounting concern is not central.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Reconcile cash returns with economic asset replacement and accounting estimates.
claims.reason: Cash economics ultimately matter, but depreciation estimates affect reported margins and can obscure replacement spending or impairments. The issues are related rather than mutually exclusive.
claims.next_check: Reconcile cash returns with economic asset replacement and accounting estimates.

assumptions: Useful-life estimates affect expense timing but not the initial cash purchase.
proof.proof: Changing depreciation does not create cash at purchase. Yet future replacement outlays depend on actual useful life, so an incorrect life estimate can also mislead a forecast of sustainable cash returns.
proof.derivation: Changing depreciation does not create cash at purchase. Yet future replacement outlays depend on actual useful life, so an incorrect life estimate can also mislead a forecast of sustainable cash returns.

claims.claim: Investors favor public investment banks for the M&A cycle while discounting private-credit concerns at alternatives managers.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare fee outlooks, flows, credit exposures and valuation changes.
claims.reason: Relative returns do not by themselves identify motivations or every driver.
claims.next_check: Compare fee outlooks, flows, credit exposures and valuation changes.

claims.claim: CoreWeave results show strong demand but construction delays and communication problems expose execution risk.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track available capacity, customer starts, penalties and financing.
claims.reason: The distinction between one facility and a provider needs the original call. Backlog is not delivered revenue, and valuation amplifies surprise risk.
claims.next_check: Track available capacity, customer starts, penalties and financing.

claims.claim: Consensus expects CoreWeave profitability in 2027 at a high forward multiple.
claims.speaker: Analyst consensus, reported by Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare the original forecast with future reported diluted earnings.
claims.reason: This is reported analyst consensus, not an Eisman forecast; the 2027 endpoint is incomplete.
claims.next_check: Compare the original forecast with future reported diluted earnings.

claims.claim: A slowdown in AI cloud demand could turn a growing competitive field into a market-share price fight.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track utilization, renewal pricing, contract terms and capacity additions.
claims.reason: The mechanism is conditional and has no specified demand threshold or date.
claims.next_check: Track utilization, renewal pricing, contract terms and capacity additions.

claims.claim: Cisco benefits from AI networking but legacy businesses dilute its overall growth relative to Arista.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare relevant product growth, margins and the total-company mix.
claims.reason: A matched segment and organic-growth analysis is needed to isolate legacy mix from execution and acquisitions.
claims.next_check: Compare relevant product growth, margins and the total-company mix.

claims.claim: Paramount savings matter, but a Warner transaction is the larger strategic variable.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare standalone cash flows, integration costs and transaction terms.
claims.reason: This is a priority judgment; it does not predict a completed transaction at a stated price.
claims.next_check: Compare standalone cash flows, integration costs and transaction terms.

claims.claim: Disney streaming improvement is offset by declining legacy media, making Netflix a cleaner story.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare segment earnings, capital needs and valuation consistently.
claims.reason: Segment offsets can be measured, but cleaner does not itself justify any premium multiple. The garbled EPS comparison is not scored.
claims.next_check: Compare segment earnings, capital needs and valuation consistently.

claims.claim: Circle strong operations can still disappoint if expected expenses rise.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Reconcile recurring profit, spending plans and pre-release expectations.
claims.reason: This is an earnings-expectations mechanism rather than proof that expenses alone caused the stock move.
claims.next_check: Reconcile recurring profit, spending plans and pre-release expectations.

claims.claim: A large share unlock may pressure Circle, while its earnings beat should lift next-year consensus.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Compare actual insider sales, float and revisions rather than equate unlock with selling.
claims.reason: Eligible shares are not automatically shares sold, and a consensus revision needs dated estimate data.
claims.next_check: Compare actual insider sales, float and revisions rather than equate unlock with selling.

claims.claim: Stablecoin competition will turn on who establishes durable distribution and market share.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track circulation, real payment use, unit economics and redemption reliability.
claims.reason: This is a research framework without a named winner, threshold or horizon.
claims.next_check: Track circulation, real payment use, unit economics and redemption reliability.

claims.claim: Rising announced M&A volume is a leading indicator for the advisory cycle, while closed volume records realized activity.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Track completion probabilities, deal mix, fee rates and closing lag.
claims.reason: The distinction is useful, but the proprietary Dealogic charts are not independently reproduced here and announced deals can fail or have different fee rates.
claims.next_check: Track completion probabilities, deal mix, fee rates and closing lag.
